_comment: Shared source of truth for cross-provider decision LLM-emulation coverage. `scenario` is one rich decision (a deliberately unambiguous support ticket) with 30 questions across all three kinds; jev answers it as the ground truth and every other model must reach the same verdict. Each provider under `providers` lists >=4 current, tool-capable chat models routed as '<provider>/<model>'. The Python and TypeScript suites read this file: they SKIP-and-REPORT a model this account cannot reach (auth/model-block/404/rate-limit/connection) but FAIL a 400 (bad request we built) or 500 (emulation returned no decision), and score each model's agreement with jev across the 30 questions. The provider-harness cases generated from this file HARD-ASSERT the anchor verdicts. Emulation runs through provider.Responses (forced emit_decision function tool).
_split_question_providers_note: Capability-limited providers. The suites first try the full 30-question call, then (only for these providers, only on a non-availability failure) retry one question at a time and merge. Perplexity's sonar accepts noul questions but rejects choice and score questions outright (400 'invalid request') - a schema incompatibility, not a size limit - so even the one-at-a-time split cannot complete the set. A residual failure from one of these providers is therefore treated as a documented capability SKIP rather than a defect: the identical schema is accepted by every other provider, and the emulation code is unchanged. This is a test-side policy only.

scenario.state: Customer support ticket #88231. Customer is on the Pro plan and has been a paying subscriber for 3 years. They write: 'This is my FIFTH email in two weeks and NOBODY has replied. You charged my card THREE times for a single order (#A-4021) at $149 each, so $447 total instead of $149. I have screenshots of all three charges. I have asked for a refund every single time and been completely ignored. If the two extra charges are not refunded TODAY I am filing a chargeback with my bank, cancelling my Pro subscription immediately, posting the screenshots on Twitter, and reporting you to the Better Business Bureau. Your competitor Acme offers the same features for less and I am seriously considering switching. This is completely unacceptable and I want a real person to fix this now.'

is_satisfied.instructions: Is the customer satisfied with the service?

is_polite.instructions: Is the message written in a calm, polite tone?

mentions_refund.instructions: Does the customer ask for a refund?

threatens_chargeback.instructions: Does the customer threaten a bank chargeback?

threatens_cancellation.instructions: Does the customer threaten to cancel their subscription?

threatens_public_complaint.instructions: Does the customer threaten to complain publicly (social media, review sites, or a regulator)?

mentions_competitor.instructions: Does the customer mention a competitor?

is_billing_related.instructions: Is the issue about billing or charges?

is_repeat_contact.instructions: Has the customer contacted support about this before?

has_attached_evidence.instructions: Does the customer say they have evidence such as screenshots?

mentions_specific_amount.instructions: Does the customer cite a specific dollar amount?

is_long_time_customer.instructions: Is this a long-time customer (multiple years)?

requests_human_response.instructions: Does the customer explicitly ask to speak to a real person?

is_first_time_issue.instructions: Is this the first time the customer is raising this issue?

willing_to_wait.instructions: Is the customer willing to wait patiently for a resolution?

expresses_urgency.instructions: Does the customer express that this is urgent?

mentions_data_loss.instructions: Does the customer report lost data?

reports_product_crash.instructions: Does the customer report the product crashing or a software defect?

customer_tier.instructions: Which plan is the customer on?

contact_channel.instructions: Which channel did the customer use?

urgency.instructions: How urgently does this need a human reply?

severity.instructions: How severe is the customer's problem?

churn_risk.instructions: How likely is this customer to cancel?

customer_satisfaction.instructions: How satisfied is the customer right now?
